original_question: Let (X, omega) be a compact Kahler manifold, and let mu be a probability measure that is locally dominated by Monge-Ampere measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions. Determine whether there exists phi in PSH(X, omega) intersect L^infty(X) such that mu = MA(phi).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target problem essentially verbatim: it has the correct ambient setting (a compact Kähler manifold), the correct unknown (a bounded ω-plurisubharmonic function), the correct measure-theoretic hypothesis on μ, and the exact existence question μ = MA(φ).
missing_details: The paper uses the normalized Monge–Ampère operator on a compact Kähler manifold: for bounded ω-psh functions v, MA(v) is the normalized measure V^{-1}(ω + dd^c v)^n, where V = ∫_X ω^n.

The phrase "locally dominated by the Monge–Ampère measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions" is not self-contained as written; the paper immediately states the equivalent precise condition that there exist u ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ L^∞(X) and C > 0 such that μ ≤ C MA(u).
To make the question fully stand-alone, μ should be stated explicitly as a probability measure on X.

The nearby context shows that such a μ does not charge pluripolar sets, so by the cited range theorem there is already a unique finite-energy solution φ ∈ E(X, ω) with MA(φ) = μ; the unresolved point is whether that φ is bounded below (hence bounded on compact X).
If one wants completely explicit notation, one should say that PSH(X, ω) means the set of ω-plurisubharmonic functions on X.
refined_question: Let (X, ω) be a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension n, and let V := ∫_X ω^n. Suppose μ is a probability measure on X which is locally dominated by Monge–Ampère measures of bounded plurisubharmonic functions; equivalently, assume there exist u ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ L^∞(X) and C > 0 such that μ ≤ C·MA(u), where for bounded ω-plurisubharmonic v one sets MA(v) := V^{-1}(ω + dd^c v)^n. Must there exist φ ∈ PSH(X, ω) ∩ L^∞(X) such that μ = MA(φ)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypothesis on μ, the paper notes that there exists a unique finite-energy function φ ∈ E(X, ω) with MA(φ) = μ; is this φ necessarily bounded below (and therefore bounded on X)?
justification: This is exactly the problem stated as Question 15 in §2.3 (p. 8). The draft already reproduces its main wording. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to make the compact-manifold normalization of MA explicit and to unpack the hypothesis on μ using the equivalent domination condition μ ≤ C MA(u), which the discussion immediately after Question 15 supplies on the same page. The surrounding context in §2.1 defines the normalized Monge–Ampère operator and the finite-energy class E(X, ω), and Theorem 2.3 together with the discussion after Question 15 explains why the remaining issue is boundedness from below of the finite-energy solution rather than mere existence.
